distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer clinical disease leaf for the full spectrum of HELLP syndrome. Antepartum, intrapartum, postpartum, partial, complete, hypertensive, normotensive, DIC-complicated, hepatic-hematoma, renal, pulmonary, neurologic, placental-insufficiency, and fetal-compromise presentations are represented as mechanisms, axes, event hazards, treatment modifiers, or future subtype layers rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: This leaf represents the HELLP microangiopathic-hepatic syndrome itself. Preeclampsia/eclampsia, DIC, TTP, complement-mediated TMA, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, viral/toxic hepatitis, sepsis, placental abruption, and postpartum hemorrhage remain separate leaves or event manifolds when they are independently present; vector-field superposition should be used rather than double-counting the same platelet, hemolysis, liver-enzyme, renal, or coagulation axes.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Ranking may consume pregnancy or postpartum context, gestational age, hypertension or absent hypertension, proteinuria or absent proteinuria, thrombocytopenia, hemolysis markers, AST/ALT/LDH, right-upper-quadrant or epigastric pain, nausea/vomiting, creatinine/urine output, coagulation markers, pulmonary edema, neurologic symptoms, fetal distress, and placental-abruption evidence when observed. Treatment response, operative findings, and final obstetric adjudication remain confirmatory unless a post-workup mode explicitly consumes them.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 胎盤虚血・抗血管新生シグナル
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Placental malperfusion and anti-angiogenic/inflammatory placental signaling create the upstream pregnancy-specific driver for most HELLP physiology; after delivery this driver usually falls, but maternal endothelial and hepatic injury may transiently worsen postpartum.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 全身性内皮障害・補体増幅
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Diffuse maternal endothelial activation, complement amplification, vasospasm, capillary leak, and platelet adhesion link placental disease to hypertension, renal endotheliosis, pulmonary edema, cerebral irritability, and microangiopathy.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 血小板・フィブリン微小血管障害
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Activated endothelium and coagulation surfaces drive platelet adhesion, platelet consumption, and platelet-fibrin microthrombi, producing the low-platelet component of HELLP and predisposing to renal, hepatic, placental, and cerebral ischemic injury.

Red cells fragment while traversing narrowed platelet-fibrin microvasculature, causing schistocytes, LDH rise, haptoglobin consumption, indirect bilirubin rise, and anemia; this is mechanical rather than immune hemolysis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 肝類洞障害・被膜伸展
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Periportal and sinusoidal fibrin deposition, ischemia, and hepatocyte injury elevate AST/ALT/LDH and produce epigastric or right-upper-quadrant pain; severe focal injury can progress to subcapsular hematoma or hepatic rupture.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 妊娠高血圧性血管ストレス
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Hypertensive and preeclamptic physiology is common in HELLP and raises cerebral, renal, pulmonary, and placental hazard, but HELLP can occur with mild or absent sustained hypertension and with variable proteinuria.

Most uncomplicated HELLP has thrombocytopenia with relatively preserved PT/aPTT, but severe disease, abruption, hepatic rupture, hemorrhage, or shock can transition into consumptive coagulopathy with low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, and major bleeding.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: 毛細血管漏出・臓器障害
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Endothelial leak, microthrombi, vasospasm, hemolysis, and hepatic dysfunction can combine to produce AKI, oliguria, pulmonary edema, hypoxemia, lactate elevation, and shock physiology.
Placental vascular disease and maternal endothelial dysfunction can reduce fetal reserve, produce fetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios, fetal distress, abruption, or fetal demise.

Vasospasm and hypertensive pregnancy physiology raise diastolic pressure in many HELLP patients.

Shock, hemorrhage, severe hepatic injury, and microvascular ischemia can raise lactate.
Chronic placental malperfusion can restrict fetal growth.
Reduced placental perfusion and fetal renal perfusion can reduce amniotic fluid.
Reduced fetal reserve can manifest as nonreassuring fetal status.
Placental vascular disease and hypertension increase abruption hazard.
Severe placental insufficiency, abruption, or maternal shock can lead to fetal demise.
Severe thrombocytopenia and microangiopathy raise maternal hazard through bleeding, hepatic, renal, cerebral, and placental complications.
Hepatic hematoma, rupture, hemorrhage, and severe liver injury are major acute maternal hazards.
Pulmonary edema, AKI, shock physiology, hypoxemia, and multi-organ failure raise maternal hazard.
DIC and major bleeding sharply raise maternal mortality hazard.

axes.display_name: 妊娠中または産褥期あり
axes.shape_free_text: Current pregnancy, intrapartum state, or postpartum state in which HELLP can manifest.
axes.required_context_rationale: This disease manifold requires active pregnancy or postpartum/peripartum context; without that context, nonspecific abdominal pain, hypertension, hemolysis, liver injury, fever, or shock should not make it rank high.

Gestational age when HELLP is antepartum or intrapartum; HELLP is most typical after mid-pregnancy but can present postpartum.
Days since delivery when HELLP presents postpartum; postpartum presentation is often within the first week but later recognition can occur.
Context score for maternal-fetal deterioration making prompt delivery/source control more urgent.

axes.display_name: 早産児肺成熟コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Probability/context that fetal lung maturation support is relevant because preterm delivery is likely.
Systolic blood pressure; HELLP often has hypertension but can occur with only mild or atypical blood pressure elevation.

Severe-range systolic or diastolic blood pressure.

Severity of headache when present.

axes.display_name: 意識・精神状態異常あり
axes.shape_free_text: Confusion, somnolence, coma, or other mental status abnormality from cerebral edema, hemorrhage, hypoxemia, hepatic/renal dysfunction, or shock.
Abdominal pain as the parent symptom for epigastric or right-upper-quadrant HELLP pain localization.
Epigastric localization of abdominal pain, often reflecting hepatic capsular involvement.
Severity of epigastric pain when present.

Severity of right-upper-quadrant pain when present.
Right-upper-quadrant tenderness on examination.
Severity of right-upper-quadrant tenderness when present.
Nausea during HELLP hepatic/systemic illness.
Vomiting during HELLP hepatic/systemic illness.

Platelet count; HELLP commonly falls below 100, with partial or evolving disease sometimes above this threshold.
Hemoglobin may fall from microangiopathic hemolysis, bleeding, hemodilution, or delivery-related blood loss.
Schistocytes on peripheral smear from microangiopathic hemolysis; usually present but can be less dramatic than classic TTP.
LDH rises from hemolysis, hepatic injury, and tissue ischemia; HELLP diagnostic frameworks often use elevated LDH.
Haptoglobin decreases with intravascular hemolysis.
Total bilirubin may rise from hemolysis and hepatic dysfunction; often modest unless severe hemolysis, hepatic injury, or cholestasis coexists.

AKI by creatinine rise, oliguria, or need for renal support.

Urine output; oliguria suggests renal hypoperfusion or AKI.

aPTT is usually preserved in isolated HELLP but can prolong with overt DIC or factor depletion.

Lactate rises with shock, hemorrhage, severe hepatic injury, or tissue hypoperfusion.
Clinical bleeding from thrombocytopenia, DIC, delivery, surgery, abruption, or hepatic rupture.

Treatment context indicating active major bleeding or high immediate bleeding-control priority.
Treatment context for severe bleeding risk from thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, surgery, abruption, or hepatic injury.
Acute major bleeding hazard from thrombocytopenia, DIC, abruption, operative delivery, or hepatic rupture.
Intracranial hemorrhage hazard from severe hypertension, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, or seizure-related trauma.

axes.display_name: 脳卒中・頭蓋内出血ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Combined cerebrovascular hazard from severe hypertension and bleeding vulnerability.
Pulmonary edema by exam, oxygenation, chest imaging, or clinical assessment.
Extent or severity of pulmonary edema when present.
Hazard of developing clinically significant pulmonary edema.
Peripheral oxygen saturation; falls with pulmonary edema, ARDS, aspiration, hemorrhage, or shock.
Hazard of overt disseminated intravascular coagulation in severe or complicated HELLP.

axes.display_name: 肝被膜下血腫ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Hazard of hepatic subcapsular hematoma from severe hepatic sinusoidal injury and thrombocytopenia.
Hazard of hepatic rupture with hemoperitoneum, often following subcapsular hematoma.

axes.display_name: 常位胎盤早期剥離ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Hazard of placental abruption from placental vascular disease and hypertension.
Nonreassuring fetal status or fetal distress when fetus is in utero.
Fetal growth restriction when chronic placental insufficiency precedes HELLP.
Oligohydramnios from placental insufficiency.

axes.display_name: 重症容量過負荷リスク
axes.shape_free_text: Risk that transfusion, plasma, crystalloid, or renal failure will worsen pulmonary edema or volume overload.

axes.display_name: 硫酸マグネシウム中毒リスク
axes.shape_free_text: Risk of magnesium accumulation or respiratory depression, mainly increased by renal impairment or reduced monitoring capacity.
Hazard of eclamptic seizure in HELLP with hypertensive or cerebral endothelial involvement.
Serum glucose relevant to corticosteroid toxicity, diabetes background, and critical illness.
Treatment context for infection vulnerability from diabetes, critical illness, invasive lines, surgery, or corticosteroid exposure.

axes.display_name: 処置関連出血ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Bleeding hazard from central line, dialysis catheter, neuraxial procedure, embolization, surgery, or operative delivery in thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy.

axes.display_name: 血栓イベントハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Macro- or microthrombotic event hazard from endothelial activation, platelet/fibrin microangiopathy, antiphospholipid background, or inappropriate procoagulant pressure.

axes.display_name: HELLP症候群の母体死亡ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Lifespan outcome hazard for maternal mortality in HELLP syndrome, driven by hepatic rupture, hemorrhage, DIC, stroke, pulmonary edema, renal failure, shock, and delayed control of the disease driver.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Falling platelets raise bleeding hazard, especially around delivery, surgery, abruption, or hepatic injury.
Severe thrombocytopenia increases hepatic bleeding/hematoma risk when hepatic injury is active.
Marked AST elevation reflects hepatic injury severity and raises concern for hematoma when paired with pain or thrombocytopenia.
New or severe RUQ pain is a clinical warning signal for hepatic capsular stretch or hematoma.
Subcapsular hematoma is the main precursor state for hepatic rupture.
Hepatic rupture produces hemoperitoneum and hemorrhagic shock risk.
INR prolongation indicates factor depletion or hepatic synthetic failure and raises bleeding hazard.
Low fibrinogen in pregnancy is strongly concerning for abruption/DIC and major bleeding.
Marked fibrin turnover supports DIC transition when paired with falling fibrinogen or prolonged PT/aPTT.
Creatinine rise marks AKI in HELLP and modifies magnesium, fluid, and transfusion risk.
Oliguria is a direct clinical marker of renal hypoperfusion or AKI.
Pulmonary edema reduces oxygenation.
Severe-range blood pressure raises seizure hazard even though HELLP can be atypical.
Severe hypertension raises stroke and intracranial hemorrhage hazard.
Eclamptic seizure increases acute maternal hazard through hypoxemia, aspiration, trauma, and cerebrovascular injury.
Major bleeding, especially hepatic rupture, DIC, surgical bleeding, or abruption, increases maternal mortality hazard.
Severe pulmonary edema or hypoxemia increases maternal hazard.
Overt DIC increases bleeding, thrombosis, organ failure, and maternal mortality hazard.
Abruption exposes tissue factor and can trigger consumptive coagulopathy.
Abruption acutely reduces fetal oxygen delivery and raises fetal distress likelihood.
Persistent fetal distress can progress to fetal demise when delivery or maternal stabilization is delayed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Worsening maternal platelets, liver injury, DIC, renal failure, pulmonary edema, neurologic symptoms, abruption, or fetal distress increases the expected benefit of prompt source control.
Gestational age changes fetal prematurity risk but does not remove the placental driver from the maternal disease geometry.

side_effects.interpretation: Operative or delivery-associated bleeding risk is higher when platelets, fibrinogen, or hepatic integrity are poor.
Preterm delivery creates neonatal prematurity risk context.

treatments.context_specific_role: Removes the pregnancy/placental driver of HELLP while requiring maternal-fetal stabilization, route planning, and hemorrhage readiness.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Neurologic symptoms, severe hypertension, or seizure increase the value of reducing seizure stochasticity.
Renal impairment or limited monitoring increases magnesium accumulation risk.

side_effects.interpretation: Toxicity risk rises when renal function is impaired or dosing/monitoring is not adjusted.

treatments.context_specific_role: Lowers seizure hazard in the HELLP/preeclampsia/eclampsia physiology without removing the placental or hepatic microangiopathic driver.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe-range blood pressure increases the need to reduce cerebrovascular and cardiac stress.

side_effects.interpretation: Maternal hypotension or fetal bradycardia context can complicate dosing.

treatments.context_specific_role: Pushes blood pressure down to reduce cerebrovascular hazard while delivery and disease control proceed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe-range blood pressure increases expected benefit of rapid pressure reduction.

side_effects.interpretation: Vasodilatory headache may confound neurologic warning symptoms.

treatments.context_specific_role: Pushes blood pressure down with oral or short-acting acute dosing pathways depending on clinical context.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe-range hypertension raises the need for acute blood pressure control.

side_effects.interpretation: Overshoot hypotension can transiently worsen perfusion markers if not titrated.

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative acute blood pressure push vector when severe hypertension is present.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active bleeding or urgent invasive procedure increases the benefit of transient platelet support.
Very low platelets increase procedural and spontaneous bleeding hazard.

side_effects.interpretation: Blood product volume can worsen pulmonary edema, especially with renal impairment.
Theoretical microthrombotic pressure can increase if platelets are given without bleeding or procedural need.

treatments.context_specific_role: Temporarily raises platelet count for bleeding control, operative delivery, anesthesia/procedure planning, or severe thrombocytopenia while HELLP source control proceeds.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hemorrhage increases benefit of restoring oxygen-carrying capacity.
Pulmonary edema or renal failure limits transfusion volume tolerance.

side_effects.interpretation: Transfusion can worsen pulmonary edema or hypertension-sensitive volume status.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supports oxygen delivery during hemolytic anemia or hemorrhage; it does not stop HELLP microangiopathy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Plasma/fibrinogen support is most coherent when factor depletion contributes to bleeding or urgent procedure risk.
Large-volume plasma can worsen pulmonary edema or renal failure.

side_effects.interpretation: Plasma volume can worsen pulmonary edema in endothelial leak or renal failure.

treatments.context_specific_role: Corrects consumptive coagulopathy or fibrinogen depletion during bleeding/procedure contexts; it is supportive and must be paired with control of the HELLP/obstetric driver.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Likely preterm delivery increases fetal lung maturity relevance.
Maternal instability may leave little time for fetal maturation effect.

side_effects.interpretation: Steroid-associated hyperglycemia can occur, especially with diabetes.

treatments.context_specific_role: Modifies fetal prematurity risk when preterm delivery is expected; it is not modeled as removing the maternal HELLP driver.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Some protocols use corticosteroids to accelerate platelet/liver enzyme recovery, but maternal outcome effect is uncertain.
Hyperglycemia and infection vulnerability limit benefit.

side_effects.interpretation: High-dose steroids can cause substantial hyperglycemia.
Immunosuppression and hyperglycemia can increase infectious risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct that can reshape laboratory recovery in selected contexts; it is not the causal source-control vector.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Observed pulmonary edema increases the value of oxygen, fluid restriction, diuresis, and ventilatory support.
Renal impairment changes diuretic response and fluid strategy.

side_effects.interpretation: Over-diuresis or hypotension can worsen renal perfusion.

treatments.context_specific_role: Stabilizes oxygenation and volume status while HELLP disease control and delivery/source control proceed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe AKI with refractory volume, electrolyte, uremic, or acid-base complications increases value of renal replacement support.
Catheter placement and anticoagulation strategy are constrained by thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy.

side_effects.interpretation: Dialysis catheter placement can bleed in thrombocytopenia or DIC.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supports renal and volume complications; does not remove placental or endothelial disease activity.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Rupture or expanding hematoma makes hemostatic intervention central to survival.
Coagulopathy makes intervention riskier but also more necessary when bleeding is uncontrolled.

side_effects.interpretation: Intervention itself can bleed in coagulopathy but may be necessary for source control.

treatments.context_specific_role: Controls life-threatening hepatic hematoma or rupture by embolization, packing, surgical repair, or transplant-center escalation depending on anatomy and stability.

risk_factors.display_name: HELLPまたは妊娠高血圧腎症の既往

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises recurrence prior and can make surveillance context more sensitive to early platelet, liver enzyme, or blood pressure shifts.

risk_factors.display_name: 妊娠高血圧性疾患コンテキスト

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises prior for HELLP and amplifies cerebrovascular, renal, and placental hazard.

present.clinical_rationale: Chronic hypertension raises baseline blood pressure and superimposed preeclampsia/HELLP risk; avoid double-counting if chronic hypertension is modeled as a full disease manifold.

present.coupling_modulation: Raises renal complication vulnerability and makes creatinine/proteinuria less specific unless CKD background is adjusted.

present.trajectory_modulation: Higher placental mass and placental stress raise hypertensive pregnancy disorder and HELLP risk.
Pregestational or gestational diabetes raises placental and vascular complication risk and increases steroid hyperglycemia toxicity.

risk_factors.display_name: 自己免疫・抗リン脂質抗体背景

present.clinical_rationale: Autoimmune and antiphospholipid contexts increase placental vascular complications and are important TMA mimics; model coexisting CAPS/SLE/TMA by superposition rather than folding them into HELLP.
Obesity raises hypertensive pregnancy risk and cardiopulmonary/anesthetic vulnerability.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises vascular and hypertensive pregnancy disorder prior.
Raises prior risk for hypertensive pregnancy disorders that overlap with HELLP.
Raises placental and hypertensive pregnancy disorder risk context.

present.coupling_modulation: Makes AST/ALT less specific for HELLP and increases bleeding/synthetic-failure vulnerability if severe.

supportive_care: 妊娠週数、分娩後日数、血圧推移、尿蛋白、血小板、AST/ALT、LDH、ハプトグロビン、ビリルビン、末梢血破砕赤血球、Cr、尿量、PT/APTT、フィブリノゲン、Dダイマーを時刻付きで保持する。
心窩部痛・右季肋部痛・右季肋部圧痛は腹痛の satellite として扱い、痛みの存在と局在・重症度を同じ事実として二重計上しない。
HELLP、妊娠高血圧腎症/子癇、TTP、補体介在性TMA、DIC、急性妊娠脂肪肝、肝炎、敗血症、胎盤早期剥離は近接 mimic として公平に残し、ADAMTS13・補体・凝固・肝機能・胎児/胎盤所見で分離する。
分娩後も血小板・AST/ALT・LDH・腎機能・肺水腫・出血リスクが一過性に悪化し得るため、胎盤娩出を即時の全軸正常化として扱わない。
重度の右季肋部痛、ショック、急な Hb 低下、AST/ALT 急上昇、肩放散痛、腹膜刺激を伴う場合は肝被膜下血腫/肝破裂ハザードを上げ、画像・輸血・IVR/外科支援コンテキストに接続する。
低血小板やDICがある場合、輸血・分娩経路・麻酔・中心静脈/透析カテーテルのリスクは treatment_modifier axis で調整し、薬剤や処置に固定ラベルを貼らない。
硫酸マグネシウムは seizure sigma を下げる介入であり、胎盤ドライバーや肝微小血管障害を直接消す介入として扱わない。
降圧薬は血圧と脳血管ハザードを push する介入であり、HELLP の血小板・溶血・肝障害の根本地形を単独で解消する治療として扱わない。
胎児発育不全、羊水過少、胎児機能不全、胎児死亡ハザードは母体 HELLP の outcome hazard とは別の obstetric/event axis として保持する。
基礎CKD、慢性高血圧、基礎肝疾患、自己免疫/TMA背景がある場合は background/risk modifier として使い、同じ creatinine・血圧・AST/ALT・血小板低下を別 disease manifold と二重計上しない。
